Hurricane prep and post-storm inspection for boats in Tampa Bay

Before a storm: fuel stabilized, batteries and electronics protected, lines and chafe gear set, haul-out coordinated if needed. After a storm: a mechanic checks the engine, electrical, and hull before you turn a key.

What's included

  • Pre-season checklist visit (May)
  • Named-storm prep: fuel, batteries, bilge, canvas, lines
  • Haul-out and trailer coordination
  • Post-storm inspection: engine, electrical, fuel, hull, lift and cradle
  • Water-intrusion response: oil and fuel flush, electrical drying
  • Insurance documentation photos
When

A pre-season visit in May or June; prep when a storm is forecast; inspection before the first start after any storm.

Time on site

1 to 3 hours

What it usually costs here

$150 to $400 for prep or inspection; flood-recovery work quoted.

In Tampa Bay specifically

Helene and Milton in 2024 damaged or displaced hundreds of boats from Tarpon Springs to Gulfport. The boats that were flushed within days survived; the ones started on the first sunny morning did not.

Questions we get

My boat took on water in the storm. Can it be saved?

Often, if the engine is flushed before it is started. Do not try to start it. Call first.

Do you haul boats?

We coordinate with yards and trailers; the mechanics do the mechanical prep.
